- **Items:** 10 working steps of one haircut, not a list. Shortest: step 7, products (93 words, 40 seconds); longest: step 3, the sides (899 words, nearly 8 minutes, much of it silent cutting). The order is the order of the cut (back, top, sides, front, texture, nape, products, dry, detail, style). Step one starts at 1:29, word 204. Per the spec, this structure is not to be borrowed.
- **Item shape:** the action narrated in "we're going to" form → an occasional why (fuller on top, no bulk at the ear, no poking out at the nape) → a check-in with the client. No look-to-swap turn except the one myth at 3:36 (growing it out does not make it look thicker).
- **The title's promise:** "Most Requested Haircut for Women Over 70" is never said; no age is said. "Drove All the Way From Idaho" is said at 0:22 and paid at 23:19. The cheekbone plan (0:48) is paid at 22:57 and 24:02.
- **Feelings:** of 10 steps, 4 carry a feeling: step 1 (a clean neckline feels good, her own), step 3 (nervous but excited, comfort, a bare neck), step 5 (worried her hair is thin; many people get nervous), and the styling and reveal (staying herself, hiding the face). Told mostly about the client or "a lot of people", in the moment, before and during the change.
- **Villain:** none. A common belief is the foil (3:36, growing it out to look thicker) and another at 21:48 (short hair can't be styled). No salon or stylist blame.
- **Hard words:** none. The only age references are the client's "Back in 68" (20:59) and the beehive joke (21:03).
- **CTA placement:** none spoken.
- **Ending:** the reveal, thanks to the client, a line that she hopes viewers enjoyed the change and the cheekbones, then goodbye.
- **What sets it apart from other models of its type:**
  - The emotion is live: a real woman over 70 is nervous, then trusting, then pleased, so the feelings are heard rather than described.
  - The reassurance lines are aimed at the nervous older client ("a little at a time", "it can grow back", "you're still yourself"), which is the voice to borrow.
  - It names a feeling most women in the comments share (hiding the face with hair) only at the reveal, as the reason the cut works.

## Why it works

It is slow (133 words a minute, long silent stretches) and warm: a stylist and a client over 70 who like each other, and a haircut viewers can copy. There is no spoken hook; the title carries the age and the road trip. The comments are mostly compliments to the client ("She is adorable with her new haircut." (36 likes); "She is so beautiful! Love her smile and style is perfect!!!" (26 likes)) and wishes for this stylist: "I wish I could drive to where you are!  I'm too old to drive far" (39 likes). Viewers name their own age and the cut's reach: "Fully half of the women above the age of 50ish had their hair cut into some version of the pixie." (13 likes); "I am a 69 yr old woman with fine hair but I have so much of it." (0 likes). Viewers want the products: "Tell me what you used to make her hair look thicker on" (39 likes); "A link to all products does not help" (0 likes). One blames stylists, not this one: "I feel you would finally be the person who could cut it right and not be afraid to thin it out." (0 likes).
